claim: Double Header (DH) utilizes intronic MiMIC/CRIMIC insertions to generate artificial exons for GFP mediated protein trapping or T2A-GAL4 gene trapping in vivo based on Cre recombinase to avoid embryo injections.
source: The first, Double Header (DH) utilizes intronic MiMIC/CRIMIC insertions to generate artificial exons for GFP mediated protein trapping or T2A-GAL4 gene trapping in vivo based on Cre recombinase to avoid embryo injections.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the DH technique.

claim: DH significantly increases integration efficiency compared to previous strategies.
source: DH significantly increases integration efficiency compared to previous strategies and faithfully reports the expression pattern of genes and proteins.
evidence: The abstract makes this claim about DH performance, which is supported by experimental data presented in the results.

claim: DH faithfully reports the expression pattern of genes and proteins.
source: DH significantly increases integration efficiency compared to previous strategies and faithfully reports the expression pattern of genes and proteins.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by expression pattern data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The second technique targets genes lacking coding introns using a two-step cassette exchange.
source: The second technique targets genes lacking coding introns using a two-step cassette exchange.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract describing the scarless CRISPR tagging approach.

claim: The first step of the scarless technique replaces the endogenous gene with an excisable compact dominant marker using CRISPR making a null allele.
source: First, we replace the endogenous gene with an excisable compact dominant marker using CRISPR making a null allele.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in the results with the ywing2+ marker.

claim: The second step of the scarless technique replaces the insertion with a protein::tag cassette.
source: Second, the insertion is replaced with a protein::tag cassette.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Table 2 with various protein tags.

claim: MiMIC is a Minos-based transposon that integrates a Swappable Integration Cassette (SIC) in the genome.
source: A versatile tool used for functional gene annotation in Drosophila is MiMIC, a Minos-based transposon that integrates a Swappable Integration Cassette (SIC) in the genome (Venken et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: MiMIC SICs contain a cassette nested between two attP sites that can be exchanged with any DNA sequence flanked with attB sites through RMCE by ΦC31 integrase.
source: MiMIC SICs contain a cassette nested between two attP sites that can be exchanged with any DNA sequence flanked with attB sites through Recombinase Mediated Cassette Exchange (RMCE) by ΦC31 integrase.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the MiMIC system.

claim: GFP-tagged endogenous proteins report the subcellular localization of the gene product and are functional in ~75% of tested genes.
source: The GFP-tagged endogenous proteins report the subcellular localization of the gene product and are functional in ~75% of tested genes (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Functional GFP-protein traps can be used for chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of transcription factors.
source: Importantly functional GFP-protein traps can be used for multiple assays. These include chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of transcription factors (Nègre et al., 2011), Immunoprecipitation (IP)-Mass Spectroscopy (MS) (David-Morrison et al., 2016; Neumüller et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2017), rapid conditional removal of gene products (Caussinus et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2018b; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Neumüller et al., 2012; Wissel et al., 2016) and sequestration of tagged proteins (Harmansa et al., 2017; Harmansa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Functional GFP-protein traps can be used for Immunoprecipitation (IP)-Mass Spectroscopy (MS).
source: Importantly functional GFP-protein traps can be used for multiple assays. These include chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of transcription factors (Nègre et al., 2011), Immunoprecipitation (IP)-Mass Spectroscopy (MS) (David-Morrison et al., 2016; Neumüller et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2017), rapid conditional removal of gene products (Caussinus et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2018b; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Neumüller et al., 2012; Wissel et al., 2016) and sequestration of tagged proteins (Harmansa et al., 2017; Harmansa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Functional GFP-protein traps can be used for rapid conditional removal of gene products.
source: Importantly functional GFP-protein traps can be used for multiple assays. These include chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of transcription factors (Nègre et al., 2011), Immunoprecipitation (IP)-Mass Spectroscopy (MS) (David-Morrison et al., 2016; Neumüller et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2017), rapid conditional removal of gene products (Caussinus et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2018b; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Neumüller et al., 2012; Wissel et al., 2016) and sequestration of tagged proteins (Harmansa et al., 2017; Harmansa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: Functional GFP-protein traps can be used for sequestration of tagged proteins.
source: Importantly functional GFP-protein traps can be used for multiple assays. These include chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of transcription factors (Nègre et al., 2011), Immunoprecipitation (IP)-Mass Spectroscopy (MS) (David-Morrison et al., 2016; Neumüller et al., 2012; Yoon et al., 2017), rapid conditional removal of gene products (Caussinus et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2018b; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Neumüller et al., 2012; Wissel et al., 2016) and sequestration of tagged proteins (Harmansa et al., 2017; Harmansa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: T2A-GAL4 creates a mutant allele by truncating the protein at the insertion site but also expresses GAL4 with the spatial-temporal dynamics of the targeted gene.
source: T2A-GAL4 creates a mutant allele by truncating the protein at the insertion site but also expresses GAL4 with the spatial-temporal dynamics of the targeted gene.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing T2A-GAL4 functionality.

claim: The Drosophila Gene Disruption Project (GDP) has generated and mapped 17,500 MiMIC insertion stocks.
source: Given the usefulness of MiMICs, the Drosophila Gene Disruption Project (GDP) (http://flypush.imgen.bcm.tmc.edu/pscreen) has generated and mapped 17,500 MiMIC insertion stocks (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Venken et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: The MiMIC collection includes insertions within introns for ~1860 genes.
source: This collection includes insertions within introns for ~1860 genes, each of which can be converted to a GFP-tagged protein trap and/or a T2A-GAL4 gene trap (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015b; Lee et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: CRIMIC is a Cas9/CRISPR Homology Directed Repair (HDR) mediated approach that integrates a modified SIC in a coding intron of choice.
source: To that end, we recently developed CRIMIC (CRISPR mediated Integration Cassette); a Cas9/CRISPR Homology Directed Repair (HDR) mediated approach that integrates a modified SIC (attP-FRT-SA-T2A-GAL4-polyA-FRT-attP) in a coding intron of choice.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: CRIMIC expands the number of genes that can be tagged using MiMIC-like technology from 1860 to ~6000.
source: This approach greatly expands the number of genes that can be tagged using MiMIC-like technology from 1860 to ~6000 (Lee et al., 2018a) allowing about forty percent of Drosophila protein coding genes to be targeted with SICs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: RMCE cassettes can be injected into embryos as part of a circular plasmid or can be circularized in vivo from an initial insertion locus in the genome through Cre/loxP or Flp/FRT mediated recombination.
source: RMCE cassettes can either be injected into embryos as part of a circular plasmid or can be circularized in vivo from an initial insertion locus in the genome through Cre/loxP or Flp/FRT mediated recombination (Diao et al., 2015; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to prior work.

claim: RMCE cassettes can replace a SIC in either orientation with equal probability due to inverted symmetric attP sequences.
source: Importantly, RMCE cassettes can replace a SIC in either orientation with equal probability due to inverted symmetric attP sequences.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing RMCE mechanism.

claim: Only 50% of all successful RMCE exchange events will result in protein or gene trap lines.
source: Therefore 50% of the insertions are inserted in the opposite orientation of transcription and will not be included in the mature mRNA. Hence, only half of all successful exchange events will result in protein or gene trap lines.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of previous RMCE approaches.

claim: DH combines GFP-protein traps and T2A-GAL4 gene traps in a single RMCE construct.
source: Here, we show that by combining GFP-protein traps and T2A-GAL4 gene traps in a single RMCE construct, named Double Header (DH), we significantly increased the number of productive RMCE events for MiMIC/CRIMIC containing genes to generate protein or gene trap alleles.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the DH innovation.

claim: DH contains SA-T2A-GAL4-polyA in one orientation and SA-GFP-SD in the opposite orientation.
source: In order to reduce the effort to generate these genetic tools we engineered Double Header (DH), a construct that combines the two key RMCE cassettes to replace intronic MiMICs and CRIMICs: (1) SA-T2A-GAL4-polyA (DHT2A-GAL4) which generates a gene trap that expresses GAL4 in the expression domain of the gene while typically inactivating gene function, in one orientation and (2) SA-GFP-SD (DHGFP) which generates a GFP-protein trap, in the opposite orientation.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the DH construct design.

claim: Insertion of DH via RMCE in a MiMIC in either orientation should result in two valuable reagents.
source: Hence, insertion of DH via RMCE in a MiMIC in either orientation should result in two valuable reagents.
evidence: This is stated in the results as the rationale for DH design.

claim: The DH compound RMCE cassette is flanked by two inverted ϕC31 attB sites in a vector backbone that contains mini-white.
source: This compound RMCE cassette is flanked by two inverted ϕC31 attB sites in a vector backbone that contains other features including mini-white as shown in Figure 1A.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The presence of white in the plasmid backbone allows for a counter selection against the integration of the whole plasmid when incorporated into a white- background.
source: The presence of white in the plasmid backbone allows for a counter selection against the integration of the whole plasmid when incorporated into a white- background, ensuring that only the DNA between the attB sites integrates.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the DH construct features.

claim: Three different DH plasmids were generated for each of the three possible codon phases (phase 0, +1, +2).
source: Because exon/intron boundaries can occur at any one of three positions in a codon (phase 0,+1,+2), we generated three different DH plasmids (Sequences can be found in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results describing DH construct variants.

claim: The DH RMCE cassette is about 4.8 kB, or about 1.5 times the size of the single T2A-GAL4 cassette.
source: Given that the RMCE cassette is about 4.8 kB, or about 1.5 times the size of the single T2A-GAL4 cassette, we anticipated a lower integration rate.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the DH cassette size.

claim: On average, ~400 embryos were injected for each MiMIC line together with a plasmid that encodes the ΦC31 integrase.
source: We tested the integration efficacy by injecting 30 strains carrying a coding intronic MiMIC insertion. On average,~400 embryos were injected for each MiMIC line together with a plasmid that encodes the ΦC31 integrase.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the injection experiments.

claim: For 16 out of 30 MiMICs tested by injection, DH integration was obtained.
source: For 16 out of 30 MiMICs, we were able to isolate yellow- flies that carry a DH integration (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The orientation of DH inserts was determined in 47 out of 72 DH RMCE events by single fly PCR.
source: We determined the orientation of DH inserts through single fly PCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and determined the orientation of the cassette in 47 out of 72 DH RMCE events.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to the PCR method shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: For 6 MiMICs tested by injection, both DH orientations were obtained.
source: For 6 MiMICs we obtained both orientations and for the other 10 MiMICs we obtained one or the other orientation (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: DH injection generated a total of 22 new reagents.
source: Hence, we generated a total of 22 new reagents, increasing the overall rate of productive RMCE events by injection (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is stated in the results summarizing the injection outcomes.

claim: The integration efficiency of DH construct by injection is ~50% versus ~66% for smaller SICs.
source: Note that the integration efficiency of DH construct by injection is lower than the smaller SICs:~50% versus~66% (Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is stated in the results comparing DH to previous methods.

claim: The number of productive DH events increases tagging efficacy to 74% versus 66% for smaller SICs.
source: However, the number of productive events increases tagging efficacy somewhat as every successful event produces a useful line: 74% versus 66%.
evidence: This is stated in the results comparing DH to previous methods.

claim: DH jump-starter constructs were integrated in the genome through P-element mediated transformation.
source: We integrated the same constructs as in Figure 1A, one for each reading frame, in the genome through P-element mediated transformation.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the in vivo mobilization strategy.

claim: The RMCE cassettes in DH jump-starter transgenes can be excised from their initial landing sites by expressing Cre recombinase in germ line cells.
source: These insertions serve as jump-starter constructs because the RMCE cassettes in these transgenes can be excised from their initial landing sites by expressing Cre recombinase in germ line cells (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Jump-starter insertions were generated in second and third chromosomes for all three possible phases of DH.
source: We generated jump-starter insertions in second and third chromosomes for all three possible phases of DH and generated double balanced stocks for subsequent crosses.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the jump-starter stocks.

claim: For 12 out of 13 MiMICs tested by crossing, DH integration was obtained.
source: We tested the efficacy of integration by crosses for DH for third chromosome MiMICs. For 12 out of 13 MiMICs tested we obtained integration of DH.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the crossing experiments.

claim: The orientation of DH was determined for 48 out of 102 insertions by PCR in the crossing experiments.
source: We determined the orientation of DH for 48 out of 102 insertions by PCR.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the crossing experiments.

claim: For 6 out of 12 MiMICs tested by crossing, both DH orientations were obtained.
source: For 6 out of 12 MiMICs we obtained both orientations and for six we obtained one or the other, resulting in 18 tagged genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The genetic crossing strategy is about twice as efficient as the injection strategy in generating RMCE events (18 constructs for 13 crossed MiMICs versus 22 constructs for 30 injected MiMICs).
source: Hence, the genetic strategy is about twice as efficient (18 constructs for 13 crossed MiMICs versus 22 constructs for 30 injected MiMICs) as the injection strategy in generating RMCE events and requires significantly less effort.
evidence: This is stated in the results comparing the two DH strategies.

claim: DHT2A-GAL4 expression patterns were very similar to previously reported single T2A-GAL4 expression patterns for MI01487 (kibra), MI06794 (Lgr4), MI06872 (CG34383), MI08614 (Dgk), and MI11741 (CG12206).
source: As we selected a few MiMICs that were previously tagged with T2A-GAL4 by the Gene Disruption Project as positive controls (Lee et al., 2018a; Diao et al., 2015) (MI01487 (kibra), MI06794 (Lgr4), MI06872 (CG34383), MI08614 (Dgk), and MI11741 (CG12206), we were able to compare expression patterns obtained by DHT2A-GAL4 to expression patterns obtained by single T2A-GAL4 (http://flypush.imgen.bcm.tmc.edu/pscreen/rmce/). In all cases the expression pattern was very similar to what was previously reported (Figure 3) (Lee et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Tracheal expression of CG12206 is consistent with a previous report.
source: In addition, tracheal expression of CG12206 is consistent with a previous report (Chandran et al., 2014) and the 5HT2BT2A-GAL4 expression pattern in the adult brain matches an independently generated T2A-GAL4 (Gnerer et al., 2015) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 5HT2BT2A-GAL4 expression pattern in the adult brain matches an independently generated T2A-GAL4.
source: In addition, tracheal expression of CG12206 is consistent with a previous report (Chandran et al., 2014) and the 5HT2BT2A-GAL4 expression pattern in the adult brain matches an independently generated T2A-GAL4 (Gnerer et al., 2015) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: DHGFP insertions show consistent patterns of expression in third instar larval brains, albeit at much lower levels than the DHT2A-GAL4 insertions at the same MiMIC site.
source: In all cases, the DHGFP insertions show consistent patterns of expression in third instar larval brains, albeit at much lower levels than the DHT2A-GAL4 insertions at the same MiMIC site (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In adult brains almost no signal of DHGFP was detected, with the exception of MI15073 which shows ubiquitous expression.
source: Note that in adult brains almost no signal of DHGFP was detected, in agreement with previous observations, with the exception of MI15073 which shows ubiquitous expression, (Diao et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2018a) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neither the size nor the design of DH alters the functionality or expression patterns of the tagged genes and proteins.
source: These results indicate that neither the size nor the design of DH alters the functionality or expression patterns of the tagged genes and proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the expression pattern data.

claim: Kibra is detected in somatic follicle cell cytoplasm, including some migratory border cells.
source: Kibra is detected in somatic follicle cell cytoplasm, including some migratory border cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: 5HT2B is expressed in both somatic and germline cells including the oocyte.
source: 5HT2B is expressed in both somatic and germline cells including the oocyte.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: Lgr4 is localized to germline nurse cell nuclei and is enriched in the oocyte anterior-dorsal and ventral cortex.
source: Lgr4 is localized to germline nurse cell nuclei and is enriched in the oocyte anterior-dorsal and ventral cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: CG34383 is mostly present in follicle cells, especially in their apical domain.
source: CG34383 is mostly present in follicle cells, especially in their apical domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: Dgk is observed in nurse cell and follicle cell nuclei as well as their cytoplasm.
source: Dgk is observed in nurse cell and follicle cell nuclei as well as their cytoplasm.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: CG12206 is quite enriched in the cytoplasm of centripetal cells.
source: CG12206 is quite enriched in the cytoplasm of centripetal cells and CG9131 is present in both germ cells and follicle cells and enriched in polar cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: CG9131 is present in both germ cells and follicle cells and enriched in polar cells.
source: CG12206 is quite enriched in the cytoplasm of centripetal cells and CG9131 is present in both germ cells and follicle cells and enriched in polar cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing Figure 4 observations.

claim: GFP protein tagging with DH can be used to determine the cellular and subcellular localization of tagged proteins.
source: In summary, GFP protein tagging with DH can be used to determine the cellular and subcellular localization of tagged proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the egg chamber staining data.

claim: Targeting genes without introns by directly fusing tags in the proper reading frame has been very difficult because HDR is much less efficient than non-homologous end joining (NHEJ).
source: Targeting genes without introns by directly fusing tags in the proper reading frame has been very difficult because HDR is much less efficient than non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) (Gratz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work.

claim: HDR repairs double stranded DNA breaks using a donor template that contains two homology regions, each typically about 1000 nucleotides, which flank the desired changes.
source: HDR repairs double stranded DNA breaks using a donor template that contains two homology regions, each typically about 1000 nucleotides, which flank the desired changes.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing HDR mechanism.

claim: A 575 nucleotide regulatory region was identified that when fused to the promoter and yellow coding sequence creates a 2.9 kilobase cassette that reliably drives expression only in the wing.
source: To design a compact marker that is compatible with Golden Gate cloning we focused on the yellow gene which has well characterized enhancers (Geyer and Corces, 1987). We identified a 575 nucleotide regulatory region that when fused to the promoter and yellow coding sequence creates a 2.9 kilobase cassette that reliably drives expression only in the wing (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ywing2+ cassette is flanked by the nucleotides 'GG' and 'CC' upstream and downstream, respectively.
source: Lastly, to make the cassette removable, we flanked the SIC with the nucleotides 'GG' and 'CC' upstream and downstream of the ywing2+ marker, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the ywing2+ cassette design.

claim: Upon insertion of ywing2+, two novel Cas9 target sites are created that are not present in the endogenous sequence.
source: Upon insertion, this creates two novel Cas9 target sites that are not present in the endogenous sequence (box inset of Figure 5A), which can be used to remove the inserted cassette for final replacement via a second round of HDR.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Nine out of ten injections led to successful integration of the ywing2+ cassette.
source: We tested the efficacy of replacing the coding sequence of 10 loci with ywing2+ (Table 1). Nine out of ten injections led to successful integration of the cassette.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1.

claim: An average of ~500 embryos were injected for each gene in the ywing2+ experiments.
source: We injected an average of ~500 embryos for each gene and recovered 1 to 6 independent founder lines for a total of 22 insertion events or ~2 founder animals/gene.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the ywing2+ injection experiments.

claim: 1 to 6 independent founder lines were recovered for a total of 22 insertion events or ~2 founder animals/gene in the ywing2+ experiments.
source: We injected an average of ~500 embryos for each gene and recovered 1 to 6 independent founder lines for a total of 22 insertion events or ~2 founder animals/gene.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the ywing2+ injection experiments.

claim: Sanger sequencing confirmed the correct insertion of all but one HDR event, in which the entire plasmid backbone had been integrated.
source: Sanger sequencing confirmed the correct insertion of all but one HDR event, in which the entire plasmid backbone had been integrated.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the ywing2+ insertion verification.

claim: Seven ywing2+ insertions are homozygous lethal.
source: As shown in Table 1, seven insertions are homozygous lethal.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 1.

claim: Lethality of ywing2+ insertions mapped to the targeted locus for Nmnat, CG13390, Med27, CG11679, and ubiquilin.
source: To test whether the lethality was specific to the removal of the targeted gene, we attempted rescue of the lethality with a genomic duplication of the locus for four genes (Nmnat (Nicotinamide mononucleotide adenylyltransferase), CG13390, Med27 (Mediator complex subunit 27), and CG11679, and tested for failure to complement molecularly defined deletions for two genes (ubiquilin and Nmnat) (Zhai et al., 2006). In all cases, lethality mapped to the targeted locus showing that no second-site lethal mutations were induced in these lines.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the rescue experiments.

claim: The ywing2+ insertion in almondex (amx) produced flies that were female sterile.
source: For the gene almondex (amx), the ywing2+ insertion produced flies that were female sterile.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the amx phenotype.

claim: Female sterility was previously observed for amx and a genomic fragment previously reported to rescue female sterility likewise rescued this phenotype in amxΔCDS,ywing2+.
source: Female sterility was previously observed for amx and a genomic fragment previously reported to rescue female sterility likewise rescued this phenotype in amxΔCDS,ywing2+(Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology consortium et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work.

claim: For the gene Stub1, four positive lines were recovered; two are homozygous lethal while two are viable and fertile.
source: For the gene Stub1 (STIP1 homology and U-box containing protein 1), four positive lines were recovered; two are homozygous lethal while two are viable and fertile.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the Stub1 phenotypes.

claim: Sanger sequencing confirmed the correct insertion of the ywing2+ cassette in all four Stub1 lines.
source: Sanger sequencing confirmed the correct insertion of the cassette in all four lines, suggesting that the gene is not essential.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the Stub1 verification.

claim: Null alleles were created for nine genes using the ywing2+ knock in cassette.
source: In summary, we created null alleles for nine genes and show that the ywing2+ knock in cassette inserted precisely based on Sanger sequencing.
evidence: This is stated in the results summarizing the ywing2+ experiments.

claim: Protein tags were successfully incorporated for Nmnat, Stub1, CG11679 and Med27 but failed for amx.
source: We attempted to incorporate protein tags for five genes (Table 2). We successfully incorporated tags for Nmnat, Stub1, CG11679 and Med27 but failed for amx.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Table 2.

claim: Internally GFP-tagged Nmnat (Nmnat::GFP::Nmnat) reverted the lethality of the ywing2+ knock in allele and hence produced functional proteins.
source: Internally GFP-tagged Nmnat (Nmnat::GFP::Nmnat) and C-terminally Flag tagged CG11679 (CG11679::Flag) reverted the lethality of the ywing2+ knock in allele and hence produced functional proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the cassette swapping outcomes.

claim: C-terminally Flag tagged CG11679 (CG11679::Flag) reverted the lethality of the ywing2+ knock in allele and hence produced functional proteins.
source: Internally GFP-tagged Nmnat (Nmnat::GFP::Nmnat) and C-terminally Flag tagged CG11679 (CG11679::Flag) reverted the lethality of the ywing2+ knock in allele and hence produced functional proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the cassette swapping outcomes.

claim: The C-terminal Flag-tagged Med27 (Med27::Flag) is recessive pupal lethal, similar to the ywing2+ knock in allele, suggesting that the C-terminal Flag tag disrupts protein function.
source: However, the C-terminal Flag-tagged Med27 (Med27::Flag) is recessive pupal lethal, similar to the ywing2+ knock in allele, suggesting that the C-terminal Flag tag disrupts protein function.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the Med27 phenotype.

claim: Sanger sequencing showed that the replacement of ywing2+ with Stub1::GFP happened precisely.
source: Because the loss of Stub1 (Table 1) does not result in an overt phenotype, we cannot determine if Stub1::GFP is functional but Sanger sequencing showed that the replacement of ywing2+ with Stub1::GFP happened precisely.
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the Stub1 cassette swapping.

claim: Cas9 mediated cassette replacement occurred correctly for four out of five genes.
source: Taken together, the data indicate that Cas9 mediated cassette replacement occurred correctly for four out of five genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results summarizing the cassette swapping experiments.

claim: Nmnat is an enzyme with Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) synthase activity that also functions as a molecular chaperone.
source: Nmnat is an enzyme with Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) synthase activity that also functions as a molecular chaperone (Zhai et al., 2006; 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work.

claim: The Nmnat family is highly conserved, required for neuronal survival and protects neurons from a variety of neurodegenerative insults.
source: Additionally, the Nmnat family is highly conserved, required for neuronal survival and protects neurons from a variety of neurodegenerative insults (Ali et al., 2013; Brazill et al., 2017; Lau et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work.

claim: A previous report generated a Nmnat null allele and determined that its loss causes lethality in first instar larva.
source: A previous report generated a Nmnat null allele and determined that its loss causes lethality in first instar larva (Zhai et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to prior work.

claim: NmnatΔCDS,ywing2+ flies are homozygous first instar larval lethal, consistent with a known protein null.
source: For our structure-function analysis, we first created a null allele of Nmnat by replacing the entire coding sequence (CDS) with ywing2+, NmnatΔCDS,ywing2+ (see Table 1). The resulting flies are homozygous first instar larval lethal, consistent with a known protein null, and can be rescued by a 3 kb Nmnat transgene known to rescue the lethality associated with the loss of Nmnat (Zhai et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the results describing the Nmnat structure-function analysis.

claim: NmnatΔCDS,ywing2+ can be rescued by a 3 kb Nmnat transgene known to rescue the lethality associated with the loss of Nmnat.
source: For our structure-function analysis, we first created a null allele of Nmnat by replacing the entire coding sequence (CDS) with ywing2+, NmnatΔCDS,ywing2+ (see Table 1).
